page.layout: One page of text, with marginal notes in the right margin. Running head at top, centred, with page number at top right. Left edge shows fragments of the neighbouring page, not transcribed. Signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.l: velit offendere officium patrisfamilias, vel praecepto-
ris, dicit illud contineri modis docendi & implendi,
quos eo, quem indigitavimus, percurrit ordine.
Hæc de philosophiæ practicæ subiecto:ob-
jectum sequitur, videlicet res contingentes,
pendentes ab hominis voluntate, ut eas pos-
sit producere, vel suspendere. Græci vocant τὰ
πρακτὰ, quæ veniunt communi Juris & Justitiæ
Media hic sunt ut supra: nisi quòd tempus
pomeridianum ab Aristotele deputatum sit
studiis practicis.
Cap. L. De alphabeto philosophiæ
poëticæ.
PHilosophiæ poëticæ alphabetum itidem
habet Subjectum, Objectum & Media.
Subjectum est Homo, quoad mentem &
ingenium ποιητικὸν[?], factivum, ex peculiari
temperamento dependens.
Hic sunt principia iterum interna & externa.
Interna sunt tum prima, tum orta.
Principia interna prima sunt in viribus ani-
mi superioribus & inferioribus[?].
In superioribus; puta in intellectu, ubi est vis
partim generalis inveniendi & judicandi τὰ ποιη-
τικά, i.e. quæ arte produci possunt; partim specialis, nu-
in voluntate, ubi est appetitus & proclivitas ad τὰ ποιητικά.

page.notes: Left edge fragments (il-, o-, e-, as, o, es, etc.) belong to the neighbouring page and were not transcribed. Greek in "Δεω-λινά" (heading note and text) is doubtful: the letters are blurred. Greek "ποιητικὸν" and "ποιη-τικά" are read from a blurred scan. The mark after "inferioribus" is a smudge or stain, possibly the start of a letter, so it is marked [?]. The decorative woodcut rule under the Greek line is not text and was left out. Catchword "ποιητικά." sits at the left, not the right; it is kept as printed.
